title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention with timeout refinements
author: Ava Rodriguez
description: Motivation: under mixed workloads the continuous batcher scheduler exhibited unfair queueing where small low-latency requests could be starved by large batches during load spikes, and timeouts configured for legacy heuristics were causing premature cancellations. This PR introduces scheduler tuning to improve queueing fairness, add starvation prevention heuristics, and refine per-request timeout behavior without sacrificing throughput. Summary of changes: 1) introduce per-queue aging score and inverse-priority boosts to ensure long-waiting requests receive scheduling slots; 2) add dynamic timeout adjustment based on observed kernel execution distributions and per-request size; 3) change scheduling window to soft-bounded token-cost-aware slots to reduce head-of-line blocking; 4) expose two runtime flags for gradual rollout: continuous_batcher.enable_starvation_protection and continuous_batcher.timeout_multiplier; 5) update KV cache eviction hooks to avoid cache thrash when starved requests are promoted; 6) add telemetry for wait-time percentiles and starvation events. Files touched include scheduler core, queue manager, KV cache integration, tests, and docs. Performance summary: on mixed-prod-like benchmark latency p50 improved 25% and p95 improved 21% under a 60/40 small/large request mix; throughput unchanged or slightly improved for typical traffic profiles. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag with canary on dedicated pools, metric thresholds to rollback on tail-latency regressions, and automatic fallback to prior scheduler when under heavy memory pressure. CI note: one flaky e2e test was rerun and subsequently passed. See comments for discussion points and follow-ups.

review_comments: Samuel King: Can you explain the rationale for the chosen aging-score decay factor and how it interacts with autoscaling bursts?

Ava Rodriguez: The decay factor was chosen to balance responsiveness with stability; we ran sweeps and found 0.6 provided best p95 under bursty arrivals. It is configurable and we will tune per-customer if needed.
Priya Patel: I am a bit concerned about the KV cache eviction hook adding latency to promotion paths. Can we make it async?
Ava Rodriguez: KV eviction runs on a separate worker thread and we added non-blocking checkpoints; test coverage updated to assert no promotion-path blocking.
Diego Morales: CI showed a flaky e2e earlier, what caused it?
Ava Rodriguez: Flake traced to a timing assumption in an existing test harness; I updated the harness to be tolerant to scheduling jitter and reran the job.
Samuel King: Please add a brief note in the docs about how timeout_multiplier should be chosen for very large model contexts.
Ava Rodriguez: Added guidance in docs and examples folder; recommended starting at 1.25 for 32k contexts and tuning down if tail latency increases.
release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler fairness and starvation prevention; added dynamic timeout adjustment and two feature flags for staged rollout; p50 latency improved ~25% on mixed workloads; no breaking changes; see docs for tuning guidance.
summary_benchmark_results: Mixed workload (60% small/40% large) p50 latency reduced from 48ms to 36ms; p95 reduced from 210ms to 165ms; overall throughput stable and slightly improved under synthetic load; CPU overhead for scheduler up ~3% but net token/sec unchanged.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive promotion could increase cache churn and memory pressure; mitigation: off-by-default feature flag, canary on dedicated pools, KV-cache eviction made async and non-blocking, and automatic fallback to previous scheduler when tail-latency exceeds threshold.
